hero:
NEXT-TOKEN PREDICTION · VISUAL OVERVIEW

An LLM builds text one token at a time

Given the tokens already available, a decoder model estimates which token could come next, selects one, appends it, and repeats. Tokens are not always complete words.

04 · Medium · decoder pipeline

Embeddings → masked attention → hidden state → logits → probabilities

Easy idea: The decoder creates a hidden representation of the context, then scores possible next tokens using logits and Softmax.

Next-token distribution: p(next token | preceding tokens) = softmax(logits at final position). Each output logit scores a vocabulary token. Numerical probabilities depend on the model and prompt.

questions.figure:
05 · Medium · decoding choices

Decoding settings change the choice, even with similar model scores

Easy idea: Greedy always chooses the top candidate; sampling methods reshape or narrow choices, then draw from their remaining chances.

Sampling detail: Temperature rescales logits before Softmax. Top-K keeps the K highest-scoring tokens, while Top-P keeps the smallest probability-ranked set whose cumulative mass reaches the threshold, then renormalizes. These settings may be combined; no sampling outcome is guaranteed.

questions.figure:
06 · Advanced · training vs generation

Training has correct next-token targets; inference must use its guesses

Easy idea: Teacher forcing uses true preceding tokens during training; generation repeatedly conditions on whatever tokens the model has produced.

Parallel training: With shifted targets, positions can be scored together under a causal mask, and cross-entropy gradients update weights through backpropagation. Inference: future ground-truth tokens are unavailable, so tokens are chosen autoregressively and appended one step at a time.

questions.technicalExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Prefill Prompt K/V Cache Build; Decode Per Token KV Reuse చేస్తుంది. Long Context Cache Memory Increase; Speculative Draft Tokens Target Model Verify చేస్తుంది, Speed Hardwareపై Depend.
questions.figure:
07 · Advanced · inference engineering

Cache past attention information and reduce expensive sequential work

Easy idea: KV caching avoids recomputing past Keys and Values, while speculative decoding can reduce the number of expensive serial steps.

Production insight: Prefill processes prompt positions and constructs per-layer KV state. Decode typically generates one token per model step while reusing past Keys/Values. Long contexts increase cache memory and bandwidth costs. Efficient attention improves memory traffic; speculative decoding uses cheaper draft tokens and a target verifier, with speedups depending on acceptance rates and implementation. The original exact speculative sampling algorithm preserves the target distribution.
